b01.text: A man in his early thirties living a double life as programmer and hacker.
Lean and pale from too many hours at a computer screen.

b02.text: Wears dark clothing; the only one without sunglasses when he returns to the Matrix.

b01.text: Speaks quietly, often in questions, with a sardonic edge when frightened.

b02.text: Deflects intensity with humor, as when he dares to flip off Agent Smith.

b01.text: Falls asleep at his computer; sleeps poorly and lives alone.

b02.text: Keeps a hollowed-out copy of Baudrillard's Simulacra and Simulations to hide illicit disks.

b01.text: Thomas Anderson works as a software programmer at Meta CorTechs by day.

b02.text: By night he is Neo, one of the world's most dangerous hackers, searching for an answer he cannot name.

b03.text: He has felt his entire life that something is wrong with the world, like a splinter in his mind.

b04.text: He sells illegal software to Choi and others to fund his search for Morpheus.

b01.text: He senses something fundamentally wrong with reality but cannot identify it.

b02.text: This splinter drives him to obsessive searching, sleepless nights, and isolation.

b01.text: To learn what the Matrix is and understand what is wrong with the world.
To believe in himself and accept that he is the One through sacrifice and love, not prophecy.
Freedom and control over his own life; he explicitly rejects fate because he dislikes not being in control.
Being nobody; being out of control; the existential terror of a reality he cannot trust.
Expert computer hacker who cracked the IRS D-Base and sells illicit software.

b02.text: Learns uploaded combat skills with exceptional speed, training ten hours straight.

b01.text: His disbelief in himself and in fate blocks him from accessing his full potential.

b02.text: Cannot accept that Matrix rules can be broken until he experiences it directly.

b01.text: Direct confrontation and questioning rather than evasion.

b02.text: Chooses action over self-preservation when others are at risk.

b01.text: Deflects with humor and sarcasm when frightened or uncertain.

b02.text: Retreats into denial and vomiting when reality becomes overwhelming, as after the Construct revelation.

b01.text: Physically normal at the start, though sleep-deprived and socially isolated.

b02.text: After extraction his muscles are atrophied from lifelong disuse and must be rebuilt.

b01.text: Willing to sacrifice his own life for someone who believed in him, even without certainty.
Trinity contacts Neo through his computer and brings him to Morpheus.

b02.text: Their intimacy grows through shared danger; he asks her to promise to finish telling him what the Oracle said.

b01.text: Neo has searched for Morpheus for years; Morpheus has searched for Neo his entire life.

b02.text: Neo refuses to let Morpheus die, choosing to re-enter the Matrix against orders to rescue him.

b02.text: Neo declares his identity as Neo rather than Anderson before throwing Smith in front of a train.

b01.text: A woman in black leather, known in hacker underground for cracking the IRS D-Base.
Wears black leather and sunglasses; moves with unnatural grace and speed.
Speaks with hypnotic directness, pressing close, lips near the ear.

b02.text: Clips words short under pressure; her voice fails her when she tries to disclose the Oracle's prophecy.

b01.text: Breathes in Neo's scent while he sleeps, then pulls away before being caught.

b02.text: Clenches her fists and whispers encouragement when watching Neo attempt the jump program.

b01.text: Trinity was once searching for the same answer Neo seeks, until Morpheus found her.

b02.text: Morpheus told her she was not really looking for him but for an answer.

b03.text: The Oracle told Trinity she would fall in love with the One, a prophecy she has never disclosed.

b01.text: She carries the Oracle's love prophecy as a burden she cannot speak, trapped between hope and fear.
To protect Neo and, when the moment comes, tell him the prophecy so her love can revive him.
To speak the truth she has been physically unable to say before it is too late.
Loyalty to Morpheus and the mission; commitment to Neo that transcends duty.
That Neo is not the One and her love is for a man who will die like the five before him.
Superhuman combat speed and precision within the Matrix; can leap between rooftops.

b02.text: Can upload and absorb pilot programs for vehicles including military helicopters.

b01.text: Her voice literally fails her when she tries to tell Neo the Oracle's prophecy before his death.
Acts decisively and commands others under fire, but cannot command her own heart to speak.
Deflects Cypher's probes about her feelings by redirecting to Morpheus's authority.
Physically capable; injured during the opening chase but fights through pain.
Insists on joining Neo's suicide mission because Morpheus means more to her than to Neo.
The Oracle prophesied she would fall in love with the One; she watches Neo with growing attachment.

b02.text: Her confession of love after his death triggers his resurrection as the One.

b01.text: Trinity follows Morpheus's orders without question in the field.

b01.text: A commanding man wearing a long black coat and circular mirrored glasses.
Eyes invisible behind mirrored lenses; his smile is described as razor-thin, able to cut glass.
Speaks with the measured cadence of a teacher or prophet, using Socratic questions.

b02.text: His voice carries the unadulterated confidence of a zealot when he declares Neo is the One.

b01.text: Offers choices in binary form and frames them as irreversible.
Morpheus has spent most of his life searching the Matrix for the One, the prophesied savior.

b02.text: The Oracle told him he would find the One, but he misunderstood, believing it was about his choice rather than the One's.

b03.text: Five candidates before Neo died because Morpheus got them amped up believing in the prophecy.

b04.text: After the fifth death he lost his way, doubted everything the Oracle had said, and doubted himself.

b05.text: Then he saw Neo and his world changed; he calls it an epiphany he cannot explain.

b01.text: Five people died because he anointed them as the One out of his own need to believe.
To find, free, and prepare the One who will end the machine war and free humanity.
To be vindicated not by prophecy but by Neo's own choice to believe.
Belief with the heart and gut, not the mind; faith is not a matter of reasonability.
That he is wrong again and Neo will die like the five before him.
Master combatant inside the Matrix; faster and stronger than any freed human except Neo.

b02.text: Skilled leader and tactician who commands absolute loyalty from his crew.

b01.text: His absolute faith makes him blind to betrayal from within his own crew.

b02.text: His belief is personal and fallible, not procedural; he has been wrong before.

b01.text: Shows the door and makes the student walk through it; teaches through experience, not lecture.
Confesses his failures directly when challenged, hiding nothing from those he is trying to free.
Physically powerful until captured and tortured by Agents with mind-intrusive serum.
Sacrifices himself to protect Neo, telling Trinity that Neo is all that matters.
Morpheus broke the rule against freeing a mind after a certain age because he believed the search was over.

b02.text: He confesses his fallibility and the five dead directly to Neo, asking only for trust.

b01.text: Trinity follows his orders in the field and trusts his judgment absolutely.
Smith tortures Morpheus for Zion's access codes while Morpheus fights to hold his mind together.
Cypher delivers Morpheus to Smith, calling him a jagoff and blaming him for lying to the crew.
The Oracle told Morpheus he would find the One, and he has structured his life around that prophecy.

b01.text: A sentient program inhabiting the body of a man in a dark suit and sunglasses.
Dark suit, sunglasses, Secret Service earphone; identical in dress to Agents Brown and Jones.

b02.text: Unnatural ice-blue eyes revealed when he removes his sunglasses during Neo's interrogation.

b01.text: Speaks with machine-calm precision that occasionally cracks into rage and contempt.

b02.text: Calls Neo Mr. Anderson, denying him his chosen identity until the very end.

b01.text: Removes his earphone when he wants to speak privately, as when confessing his hatred of the Matrix.
Agent Smith is a sentient enforcement program tasked with destroying the human resistance.

b02.text: He has come to hate the Matrix, calling it a zoo, a prison, a reality he can no longer stand.

b03.text: He believes humans are a virus, a cancer, a plague, and that Agents are the cure.

b01.text: He is trapped inside the Matrix he despises, able to smell and taste its corruption but unable to leave.
To destroy Zion, end the resistance, and thereby become free of the Matrix he hates.
To escape the Matrix, but his method is control and destruction rather than transcendence.
Order, efficiency, and the elimination of the human virus from the planet.
Being trapped in the Matrix forever, saturated by its smell and stink.
Superhuman speed and strength; can punch through concrete walls and dodge bullets.
His strength and speed are based on the Matrix's rules, so he can never be as fast as the One.
Methodical pursuit; uses interrogation, betrayal, torture, and overwhelming force.
Removes his earphone and confesses his hatred to Morpheus, a moment of unauthorized vulnerability.
Functionally immortal within the Matrix until destroyed from within by the One.
From his perspective, humans are the disease and he is the cure; his logic is sympathisable.
Smith captures and bugs Neo, then hunts him to room 303 where he shoots him dead.

b02.text: Neo destroys Smith by diving into him from within after awakening as the One.

b01.text: Smith tortures Morpheus with serum and confesses his desire to escape the Matrix to him.
Smith negotiates with Cypher over steak, promising reinsertion as a rich man in exchange for Morpheus.

b01.text: A crew member of the Nebuchadnezzar who has been in the real world for nine years.
No distinctive costume notes beyond standard crew wear.
Speaks with bitter humor and sardonic one-liners, masking deep resentment.
Drinks Dozer's homemade alcohol and looks at the Matrix code, seeing only blonde, brunette, redhead.

b02.text: Sweats nervously and glances around when entering the Matrix knowing the trap is set.

b01.text: Cypher took the red pill nine years ago and has regretted it ever since.

b02.text: He has watched five candidates die believing Morpheus's prophecy and has concluded it is bullshit.

b03.text: He once thought he was in love with Trinity and used to dream about her.

b01.text: He chose truth and got nine years of cold, goop, and watching people die for a lie.
To be reinserted into the Matrix as a rich, important man with no memory of the real world.
He needs what he cannot have: the bliss of ignorance, which makes him the anti-Neo.
Comfort and self-preservation over truth and freedom; ignorance is bliss.
Dying in the real world for a cause he no longer believes in.
Competent operator who can read Matrix code and run the operator station.
His resentment makes him careless; he misses Tank with his first shot.
Conspiracy and betrayal; uses a dropped phone to signal the Agents.
Savors the steak he knows is not real, choosing sensation over truth.
Physically healthy but psychologically deteriorated after nine years of war.
He frames his betrayal as rational self-interest; he calls himself the messenger, not the enemy.
Cypher calls Morpheus a jagoff and blames him for tricking the crew into the real world.
Cypher tells Trinity he thought he was in love with her, nuzzling her comatose body.
Cypher negotiates with Smith over steak, trading Morpheus for reinsertion as someone important.
Cypher confides in Neo over drinks, revealing the five dead and advising him to run from Agents.

No jacks or plugs anywhere on his body, unlike the rest of the crew.
Warm and enthusiastic, cracking jokes as he loads programs; calls Neo buddy.
Announces Matrix entries like a flight attendant, telling crew to sit back and enjoy the flight.
Tank and his brother Dozer were born free in Zion, the last human city deep underground.

b02.text: He serves as the Nebuchadnezzar's operator, monitoring Matrix code and managing entries and exits.

b01.text: He is a genuine child of Zion who has never known the Matrix and fights for a world he believes in.
To support the mission and protect his crew; to see Morpheus's faith vindicated.
To survive Cypher's attack and save Neo and the mission from destruction.
Zion is more important than any individual, including himself, Morpheus, or Neo.
Losing his brother Dozer and the crew to betrayal.
Expert operator who can read raw Matrix code and manage all entries, exits, and program uploads.
He is physically vulnerable in the real world; Cypher's lightning rifle nearly kills him.
Works frantically at the operator station, searching for exits and tracing positions in real time.
Channels grief into action, returning to the operator station despite charred wounds.
Fully healthy until Cypher shoots him twice with a lightning rifle.
Tells Morpheus he was more than a leader, he was a father, before preparing to pull the plug.
Tank and Dozer are brothers, both born free in Zion, both serving on the Nebuchadnezzar.
Tank is Neo's operator, uploading his combat training and guiding him through the Matrix.
Cypher shoots Tank twice but Tank survives and kills Cypher before he can unplug Neo.

b01.text: An older woman who looks like someone's grandma, wearing oven mitts and comfortable slacks.
Warm, grandmotherly, and blunt; smokes cigarettes and bakes cookies while dispensing fate.
Bakes chocolate chip cookies and offers them as comfort after delivering hard news.
The Oracle has been with the resistance since the beginning and is considered a guide, not a fortune teller.

b02.text: She prophesied the return of the One, a man who could reshape the Matrix at will.

b03.text: She told Morpheus he would find the One, and told Trinity she would fall in love with the One.

b01.text: She tells each person what they need to hear, not what is objectively true, which is a burden of manipulation.
To guide individuals toward the choices that will fulfill the prophecies she has set in motion.
She needs the prophecies to be self-fulfilling through the choices they provoke, not through declaration.
Self-knowledge over certainty; she displays a plaque reading Know Thyself in her kitchen.
That the prophecies will fail if the individuals do not choose to act on what they are told.
She knows what people will do before they do it and what they need to hear to get there.
Her prophecies are self-fulfilling, not declarative; they require the subject to choose to act.
Uses everyday warmth and apparent casualness to deliver devastating prophecies without ceremony.
Apologizes sincerely when giving good people bad news, offering cookies as comfort.
Healthy and ageless within the Matrix; her nature as a program is left unexplained.
She manipulates through truth shaped to need, not through lies; her honesty is selective but genuine.
She tells Neo he is not the One but that Morpheus will sacrifice his life for him.
She told Morpheus he would find the One, anchoring his life's mission.
She told Trinity she would fall in love with the One, a prophecy Trinity has never spoken.

A tracking device used by Agents to locate targets within the Matrix.

arc.start_state: Concealed in Smith's case during interrogation
arc.end_state: Extracted from Neo and discarded on the pavement, reverted to a wire tap

b01.text: At least three Agents: Smith, Brown, and Jones, all identical in dark suits and sunglasses.
Smith appears to lead, giving orders to Brown and Jones, who follow without question.
To destroy the human resistance, capture Zion's access codes, and maintain the Matrix's control.
Can inhabit the body of anyone still hardwired to the Matrix; possess superhuman speed and strength.
Unified and obedient until Smith begins showing unauthorized emotion and anger.
Agents are sentient programs that enforce the Matrix system by hunting freed humans.

b02.text: Every freed human who has fought an Agent has died, until Neo.

awareness_of_neo.description: The Agents' awareness level of Neo as a target

arc.start_state: Enforcement programs hunting the resistance
arc.end_state: Two Agents fled in fear after Smith is destroyed by the One

b01.text: Morpheus, Trinity, Cypher, Tank, Dozer, Apoc, Switch, Mouse, and newly freed Neo.
Morpheus commands; Trinity is ranking officer; Tank operates; Dozer pilots; others are operatives.
To free minds, find the One, and ultimately end the machine war and free humanity.
The hovercraft Nebuchadnezzar, the Construct, uploaded combat skills, and hardwired phone exits.
Loyal to Morpheus and the mission, but Cypher's disillusionment fractures the group from within.
A resistance cell operating from the Nebuchadnezzar, broadcasting a pirate signal into the Matrix.

b02.text: Five previous candidates for the One died under Morpheus's guidance before Neo.

arc.start_state: Eight-person resistance cell with a newly freed ninth member
arc.end_state: Decimated crew of four survivors after betrayal and battle

b01.text: Multiple Sentinel units that hunt in packs, described as shifting shadows of mechanized death.
Deployed by the machine system; no individual hierarchy discernible.
Search and destroy; designed for one thing: killing humans in the real world.
Black alloy skin, sinewy coils, skeletal appendages, and shark-like malevolence in flight.
Attack in coordinated swarms, opening and shifting like killer kaleidoscopes.
Real-world killing machines deployed by the machine system to hunt human ships.

proximity_to_ship.description: How close the Sentinels are to the Nebuchadnezzar

arc.start_state: Distant machine hunters in the sewer mains
arc.end_state: Destroyed by EMP detonation, filling the overflow pit with cold metal carcasses

b01.text: A neural-interactive simulation generating late twentieth-century life to keep humanity docile while their bodies are harvested.

b02.text: The Matrix is everywhere, all around, visible out windows and on television, felt when going to work or paying taxes.

b01.text: Morpheus and the freed humans know the truth; everyone else is trapped inside without knowing.
Built and maintained by machines that discovered a new form of fusion using human bioelectricity.
Death in the Matrix kills the physical body because the body cannot live without the mind.

b02.text: Freed humans can bend Matrix rules through mental discipline; the One can break them entirely.

b03.text: Deja vu indicates the Matrix has been altered, a glitch that occurs when something is changed.

b01.text: The first Matrix was designed as a perfect human world but entire crops were lost because no one would accept the program.

b02.text: The Matrix was redesigned to the peak of human civilization because humans define reality through suffering and misery.

compromised.description: Whether the Matrix's integrity has been compromised by the One's awakening

arc.start_state: Machine-controlled simulation keeping humanity enslaved
arc.end_state: Compromised by the One, who sees its code and promises to show people a world without rules

b01.text: When the first man born inside the Matrix who could reshape it died, the Oracle prophesied his return.

b02.text: His coming would hail the [...] humanity.

b01.text: Morpheus believes absolutely and has spent his life searching; Cypher believes it is bullshit that got five people killed.
Established by the Oracle, whose prophecies are treated as guides rather than absolute truths.
The prophecy drives Morpheus to free minds at great risk and to sacrifice himself for Neo.

b02.text: The Oracle tells each person what they need to hear, making the prophecy self-fulfilling rather than declarative.

b01.text: A man born inside the Matrix had the ability to change [...].

b02.text: He freed the first of them and taught them the truth; when he died, the Oracle [...].

fulfillment_status.description: Whether the One prophecy has been fulfilled

arc.start_state: Ancient prophecy driving Morpheus's life mission and five deaths
arc.end_state: Fulfilled not by declaration but by Neo's choice, sacrifice, and Trinity's love

b01.text: The Oracle told Trinity she would fall in love with a man, and that man would be the One.
Trinity is the sole bearer of this prophecy and has never told anyone, including Neo.
Established by the Oracle, whose prophecies are self-fulfilling through the choices they provoke.
Trinity's confession of this prophecy after Neo's death is the trigger for his resurrection as the One.

b02.text: Nothing may reveal this connection before the death scene; its concealment structures the entire third act.

b01.text: The Oracle told Trinity the prophecy before the events of the film; Trinity has been unable to speak it aloud.

disclosed.description: Whether the love prophecy has been disclosed to Neo

fulfilled.description: Whether the love prophecy has been fulfilled through Neo's resurrection

arc.start_state: Secret prophecy burdening Trinity, unspoken and unconfirmed
arc.end_state: Confessed over Neo's dead body, triggering his resurrection and fulfilling itself
